title: Second Helping
logline: At an east-coast wedding reception, hosts keep piling food onto plates, guests protest and then accept, and one man goes back for a third helping without being asked.

object.note: Object 2 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The wedding season carries across the island: from choosing what will be worn to a reception where hosts keep filling plates, and wanting moves from the eye to the appetite.

thread_out.thread: From a feast's second and third helpings to a kitchen before the New Year, where the maker's hands no longer need to look and a child's day hangs on the first bite.

requirements: A wedding family willing to have their reception filmed
Guests willing to be filmed eating and being urged to eat
A kitchen willing to be filmed before and after the feast

suggestions.name: A wedding reception hall in Batticaloa or Trincomalee
suggestions.why: Both are established towns with active wedding-reception venues and strong hospitality traditions.
suggestions.verify: No family has been contacted; this is a plausible setting, not a confirmed location.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: A second helping can be reached for on our own or accepted because a host keeps pressing it on us, and either way it is still wanting. The texts say wanting comes feeling pleasant or just ordinary, never unpleasant.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අනුන් බල කරන නිසා හෝ අපේම කැමැත්තෙන් හෝ ගන්නා දෙවැනි පිඟාන ද ආශාවක් වන අතර, එය දැනෙන්නේ ප්‍රියජනක ලෙස හෝ සාමාන්‍ය ලෙස මිස කිසි විටෙක අප්‍රියව නොවේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma's own examples of greed-rooted minds include eating with relish, arising either spontaneously or when urged on by others or by one's own coaxing of a hesitating mind; the texts note that the prompted kind carries a certain heaviness. The compendium of feeling (vedanā) teaches that every mind tastes its object as pleasant, painful or neutral, with no fourth way. It places the joyful greed-rooted minds among the joyful ones, and finds mental displeasure only in the two aversion-rooted minds.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Hosts piling food onto plates and guests protesting, then giving in, show wanting pushed along from outside; the man who goes back for a third helping without being asked shows the same reach arising on its own. Faces at the tables, relish on some and a flat, automatic eating on others, let the viewer notice that wanting does not always look like pleasure.

key_terms.en: feeling: the tasting of an object's flavour

lesson.caution: This does not mean that being urged makes the wanting someone else's, or that the hosts' generosity is being faulted: the texts still count prompted wanting as wanting, and the film judges no one at the table.
lesson.builds_on: The last film showed wanting reached for through the eye and pushed along by a relative; here the same push comes from hosts at a feast, and the film adds that wanting always comes with a feeling tone, pleasant or flat.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
